findings.title: 13 web unit tests are failing, and nothing in the repository ever runs them
findings.evidence: `pnpm --filter @ship/web exec vitest run` -> 13 failed / 138 passed / 151 total across 3 of 16 files, reproduced identically twice (runs/web-unit-failures.log). Root script is `"test": "pnpm --filter @ship/api test"` and reports 451/451 green. No CI exists: .github/ contains only instructions/, there is no workflows/ directory and no .gitlab-ci.yml / Jenkinsfile / buildspec.yml anywhere. .husky/pre-commit runs check-empty-tests.sh, check-api-coverage.sh and `comply opensource` — it never executes a test suite.
findings.hypothesis: The sprint->week rename updated web/src (document-tabs.tsx:115-116 emits tab id 'weeks') while document-tabs.test.ts:25,34,97,114,160 still asserts 'sprints'; DetailsExtension.ts:48 changed content to 'detailsSummary detailsContent' while DetailsExtension.test.ts:16 still asserts 'block+' and builds an Editor without the sibling nodes so ProseMirror throws; useSessionTimeout.test.ts mocks fetch without the CSRF pre-flight that fetchWithCsrf performs, so apiPost throws into the force-logout catch. Every one of these is what a CI run would have caught on the introducing commit.
findings.estimatedImpact: The repo has no automated regression gate at all. Making root `test` recursive and adding a CI workflow surfaces 13 already-broken tests immediately and is the precondition for every other improvement in this category.

findings.title: 68 e2e tests (7.9%) can pass without executing a single assertion, including a security and an authorization test
findings.location: e2e/program-mode-week-ux.spec.ts (33 of 66 tests); e2e/security.spec.ts:217; e2e/authorization.spec.ts:299; e2e/context-menus.spec.ts (6); e2e/accessibility-remediation.spec.ts (6); e2e/features-real.spec.ts (5) — full list in runs/e2e-vacuous-tests.txt
findings.evidence: Brace-scanner over 866 static test blocks (runs/vacuous.mjs): 3 tests contain no expect() at all, 65 more have every expect() nested inside a conditional. 98 `if (await ...)` guards and 35 count/length comparisons across e2e/. security.spec.ts:217 loops over rendered <a> elements and asserts only `if (href?.startsWith('data:'))` — it never asserts a link was created, so zero anchors is a green test. authorization.spec.ts:299 nests `expect(response.status()).toBe(403)` inside `if (wsResponse.status() === 200)` inside `if (workspaceId)`.
findings.hypothesis: The guards were added to stop tests failing on missing seed data — the exact failure mode .claude/CLAUDE.md already forbids for test.skip(). The rule was written for test.skip() and never extended to if-guards, so the practice migrated rather than stopped. bulk-selection.spec.ts:793 shows the sanctioned pattern in the same repo.
findings.estimatedImpact: 7.9% of the e2e suite provides no signal. Two of those tests are the only automated checks for a stored-XSS vector and for member-level audit-log access.

findings.title: Retries hide a test that fails on first attempt in 100% of runs; 11 tests flaked across 3 identical runs
findings.evidence: Three identical 869-test runs at 4 workers. First-attempt failures: 8 / 5 / 3. Reported failures after retries: 1 / 0 / 1 — retries erased 7 / 5 / 2. `my-week-stale-data.spec.ts > retro edits are visible on /my-week after navigating back` failed or timed out on the first attempt in ALL THREE runs and was reported as passing all three times. 11 distinct tests produced a non-clean outcome in >=1 run; 858 of 869 were clean in all three.
findings.hypothesis: retries:1 locally was added 'for flaky WebSocket/timing tests' (config comment). It works — the suite looks green — which removes the pressure to fix underlying order-dependence, so the flake set grows. Dominant smells: shared state inside a worker's database (5 tests depend on data another test may or may not have created) and fixed short timeouts (4). The suite carries 619 waitForTimeout calls across 49 of 71 spec files.
findings.estimatedImpact: A real regression in any of these 11 paths would be retried into green. The improvement target (3 flakes fixed with root cause) is directly available here.

findings.title: Concurrent multi-client editing / Yjs merge has no test
findings.evidence: 11 tests mention collaboration/WebSocket/real-time but cover only connection establishment, a status indicator and reconnection. browser.newContext() appears in only 2 of 71 spec files (security.spec.ts, private-documents.spec.ts), neither for editing. mentions.spec.ts:374 uses browser.newPage() (same browser, sequential not concurrent), places every assertion inside `if (await option.isVisible())`, relies on waitForTimeout(2000)+waitForTimeout(3000) for sync, and first-attempt-failed in 2 of 3 runs. No test performs concurrent edits from two clients and asserts the merged result. api/src/collaboration/index.ts sits at 25.0% function coverage (7/28).
findings.hypothesis: Cross-client tests are slow and awkward, so coverage stopped at 'the socket connects'. The CRDT merge behaviour — the justification for the Yjs architecture in docs/unified-document-model.md — is verified by nothing.
findings.estimatedImpact: A Yjs or persistence regression that silently drops one client's edits would ship green. Highest-value place to spend the '3 meaningful new tests' half of the improvement target.

findings.title: Canceling an inline comment leaves an orphaned comment-highlight mark in the saved document (real app bug candidate)
findings.evidence: The only test that failed BOTH attempts, and it did so in runs 1 and 3 (passed in run 2). Failure output shows the locator resolving 14 consecutive times over a 10s window to comment that gets canceled after Escape was pressed (runs/e2e-run1-failures.txt, runs/e2e-run3-failures.txt).
findings.hypothesis: The Escape handler is bound to a .comment-pending-field <input> rendered inside a Decoration.widget and auto-focused in a requestAnimationFrame (CommentDisplay.tsx:185-188). When focus has not landed, the keypress never reaches onCancelComment -> editor.commands.unsetComment(). comment-highlight is a TipTap Mark, i.e. document content (CommentMark.ts:69), not a decoration — so the leftover span persists into documents.content and syncs through Yjs, pointing at a comment that was never created.
findings.estimatedImpact: Document-content pollution on a plausible user action (start a comment, change your mind). Cross-file to error-handling for confirmation of the focus race.

findings.title: Allocation grid returns planId: null immediately after the plan is created (read-after-write race candidate)
findings.evidence: First-attempt failure in runs 1 and 2. `expect(week1Data.planId).toBe(plan.id)` received null on a GET issued immediately after a successful weekly-plan POST in the same test, against the worker's own isolated Postgres container (so not cross-test interference).
findings.hypothesis: The grid endpoint joins plans to allocations on a key the just-created plan does not yet satisfy (week assignment written in a separate statement), so a read immediately following the write sees the allocation but not the plan.
findings.estimatedImpact: A user creating a weekly plan may see their own plan missing from the allocation grid on the next render. Cross-file to db-query / api-perf.

findings.title: Coverage measurement is broken in api and entirely absent in web and shared
findings.evidence: `pnpm --filter @ship/api test:coverage` exits 1 with "MISSING DEPENDENCY Cannot find dependency '@vitest/coverage-v8'" (runs/api-coverage-attempt.log). The package appears 0 times in pnpm-lock.yaml and in no node_modules/@vitest directory, yet api/vitest.config.ts declares provider:'v8'. web/vitest.config.ts has no coverage block and web/package.json has no test:coverage script. shared/ has no test script and 0 test files for 8 source files. Substitute NODE_V8_COVERAGE measurement (runs/api-v8-coverage.txt): api function coverage 51.4% (398/774), 7 of 79 modules never loaded. Weakest: services/ai-analysis.ts 7.1% (1/14), services/secrets-manager.ts 8.3% (1/12), services/oauth-state.ts 11.1% (1/9), routes/programs.ts 15.4% (2/13), routes/caia-auth.ts 16.7% (2/12), routes/admin-credentials.ts 18.2% (2/11), routes/weekly-plans.ts 21.4% (3/14), collaboration/index.ts 25.0% (7/28), utils/document-crud.ts 29.3% (12/41).
findings.hypothesis: The coverage block and script were added aspirationally and the provider was never installed; because nothing runs `test:coverage` in CI (TEST-1), the broken script was never exercised.
findings.estimatedImpact: No coverage-based decision is possible and no coverage movement can be proven in compare mode. The npm registry is blocked in this environment so this was reported rather than fixed; baseline mode would not install dependencies regardless.

findings.title: Two shipped routes have zero test coverage of any kind
findings.location: web/src/main.tsx:215 (/dashboard -> DashboardPage), :240 (/team/org-chart -> OrgChartPage), :222 (/projects), :216 (/my-week, target of the / redirect at :214)
findings.evidence: Grep across all 71 spec files: '/dashboard' and 'DashboardPage' -> 0 occurrences; 'org-chart'/'orgchart' -> 0 occurrences (and no unit test either). '/projects' is navigated to exactly once, document-workflows.spec.ts:162. '/my-week' — the app's landing page — appears in one spec file (my-week-stale-data.spec.ts) whose two tests are both on the flake list.
findings.hypothesis: E2E coverage grew feature-by-feature around /docs (162 navigations) and /issues (152); routes added later or reached only via redirect were never picked up.
findings.estimatedImpact: The landing page and the org chart can break with no test noticing. /dashboard does have web/src/pages/Dashboard.test.tsx — one of the 13 tests root `pnpm test` never runs (TEST-1).

findings.title: `pnpm test` TRUNCATEs whatever database DATABASE_URL points at
findings.evidence: setup.ts runs, in the beforeAll of every one of the 28 api test files, TRUNCATE TABLE workspace_invites, sessions, files, document_links, document_history, comments, document_associations, document_snapshots, sprint_iterations, issue_iterations, documents, audit_logs, workspace_memberships, users, workspaces CASCADE. client.ts:10 builds the pool from api/.env.local — the same file scripts/dev.sh writes for the dev database. No .env.test, no test-specific override. Confirmed operationally: this audit had to create a separate ship_unit_audit database before running the api suite, because running it as documented would have destroyed the 500-document seeded dataset the other audit categories depend on.
findings.hypothesis: The api suite predates the e2e testcontainers isolation and was never migrated to it; fileParallelism:false in api/vitest.config.ts is the workaround for the resulting cross-file interference.
findings.estimatedImpact: The sequence documented in .claude/CLAUDE.md (`pnpm dev`, then `pnpm test`) silently wipes the developer's dev database. It also makes the api suite order-dependent, the likeliest explanation for the one api-unit flake observed (weeks.test.ts > should accept all valid ratings (1-5) returned 404 in 1 of 7 runs).

findings.title: E2E worker auto-sizing collapses to 1 worker on macOS
findings.evidence: Worker count is derived from os.freemem(). Measured on this machine: os.totalmem() 24.0 GB, os.freemem() 0.3 GB (macOS reports nearly all RAM as used/cached/compressed), 14 CPUs -> memoryBasedLimit = floor((0.3-2)/0.5) = -4 -> Math.max(1, min(-4,14)) = 1 worker. All measurements in this report pin PLAYWRIGHT_WORKERS=4.
findings.hypothesis: os.freemem() is a meaningful signal on Linux CI runners but not on macOS, where the memory heuristic was presumably tuned by observation rather than by reading the value it computes.
findings.estimatedImpact: A developer running `pnpm test:e2e` on a Mac gets a single-worker run, roughly 4x the measured 9 minutes — a strong disincentive to run the suite locally.

findings.title: Stale test-count comment and heavy fixed-sleep usage
findings.evidence: The config comment advertises [1/641]; `playwright test --list` reports 869 specs across 71 files. `grep -rn "waitForTimeout" e2e --include='*.spec.ts' | wc -l` -> 619 occurrences in 49 files, led by tables.spec.ts (52), file-attachments.spec.ts (37), features-real.spec.ts (36), backlinks.spec.ts (34), drag-handle.spec.ts (33), data-integrity.spec.ts (33).
findings.hypothesis: Both are symptoms of a suite that grew without a gate reading it back: the comment drifted 228 tests out of date, and each new flake was answered with another sleep.
findings.estimatedImpact: Hygiene, but the waitForTimeout density is the mechanism behind TEST-3 — every fixed sleep is a flake waiting for a slower machine.
